surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Four points for MacKinnon as the Avalanche beat the Lightning
paras: Devon Toews and Nazem Kadri scored less than five minutes apart early in the first to put the Avalanche up 2-0. The second period was a wild one. Fedor Svechkov made it 3-0 just 24 seconds into the period, but Jake Guentzel got the Lightning on the board on the power play midway through the period. Artturi Lehkonen stretched the lead to 4-1 late in the period. Guentzel struck again later in the period to cut Colorado’s lead to 4-2, and the goal stood after the Avalanche challenged for a missed stoppage. Nathan MacKinnon made it 5-2 for the Avs early in the third, but Charle-Édouard D'Astous made it 5-3 with less than five minutes left. Martin Nečas added an empty-net goal with less than three minutes left to make it 6-3. MacKinnon finished with four points on a goal and three assists, and Nečas had a goal and two assists.

The score flatters the Avalanche: the Lightning had the better of the play. Replay the chances a hundred times and the Lightning win about six in ten. Mackenzie Blackwood made 31 saves for the Avalanche, and Andrei Vasilevskiy allowed five goals on 23 shots. The Avalanche improved to 6-4-1, and the Lightning fell to 7-3-0.

items.text: The Lightning’s three-game winning streak is over.
Artturi Lehkonen has a point in six straight games.
Nikita Kucherov’s six-game point streak against Colorado ended.
Nazem Kadri scored his first goal of the season, his first since Mar 30 (14 games played since).
